This page is pending SME review to merge inpatient/outpatient/ER-UC guidance into a single combined recommendation. Until that review is complete, each care setting's original content is shown separately below.
## INPATIENT:
[Help and Legend](general-information-legend)

# EXACERBATION OF CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE (COPD)

Exacerbation of COPD (ECOPD): dyspnea and/or cough and sputum worsening over

< 14 days. An acute change in one or more of the following:

- Increased cough frequency and severity

- Increased sputum volume and/or changes in character

- Increased dyspnea

Available evidence is limited but suggests antibiotics are beneficial for COPD

exacerbations in hospitalized patients. Antibiotics are strongly recommended for

all patients admitted to the ICU for COPD exacerbation and those with sputum

purulence (new or increased from baseline).

Antibiotics are not routinely recommended for non-critically ill patients with

clear non-infectious causes for exacerbations (e.g. medication non-adherence,

environmental exposures) or known viral infections.

Dyspnea differential: acute coronary syndrome, worsening heart failure,

pulmonary embolism, pneumonia, medication non-adherence

Test for influenza and COVID

# General Ward patients

Preferred:

[Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875-125 mg PO q12h R for 5 days](psjzid-amox-clav-875-125mg-po-q12h)

< OR >

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h DI for 5 days](psjzid-doxycycline-100mg-po-q12h)

< OR >

[Azithromycin 500mg PO once, then 250mg q24h days 2-5 O](orz-set-abx-azithromycin-po-500-250-once-q24h-x4days)

Unable to tolerate oral antibiotics:

[Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV q6h R for 5 days](psjizid-ampicillin-sulbactam-3gm-iv-q6h)

History of Pseudomonas in a respiratory isolate in the past year:

[Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h R for 5 days](psjizid-cefepime-2-gm-iv-q8h)

# NOTE: Fluoroquinolones are not listed as a choice because of the risk of serious

# side effects outweigh the benefits.

[Fluoroquinolones FDA Serious Adverse Reactions](orz-gtx-abx-idp-fluoroquinolones-fda-warnings)

# ICU patients

Preferred:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h R for 5 days](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)

History of Pseudomonas in a respiratory isolate in the past year or

immunosuppression:

[Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h R for 5 days](psjizid-cefepime-2-gm-iv-q8h)

< OR >

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h R for 5 days](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

## OUTPATIENT:
[Help and Legend](general-information-legend)

# BRONCHITIS

Acute bronchitis should not be treated with antimicrobials except in specific

circumstances. If pneumonia is suspected, order a chest x-ray.  If an infiltrate

is not present, the patient does not have bacterial pneumonia and need not be

treated for it. If a patient has chronic pulmonary disease, see COPD

exacerbation menu.
